title: Upgrade rate and average price increase among accounts with 2 subscriptions
prompt: Among accounts that have had exactly two subscriptions (they changed plans once), what fraction upgraded to a higher-priced plan the second time, and what's the average price increase for those who did?
population: Accounts with exactly two subscriptions, comparing the first (by started_at) to the second.
grain: Two metrics, each a single row: the upgrade rate, and the average price increase among upgraders.
metricDefinition: (a) share of two-subscription accounts where the second plan's monthly_price exceeds the first's; (b) among those, average(second price − first price).
transformationPlan: rank each account's subscriptions by started_at
take the 1st and 2nd subscription per account
join each to its plan's monthly_price
compare 2nd price to 1st price to classify upgrade vs. not
compute the upgrade rate and the average price increase among upgraders
referenceSql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT s.account_id, s.plan_id, s.started_at, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.account_id ORDER BY s.started_at) AS rn FROM subscriptions s), pivoted AS (SELECT r1.account_id, p1.monthly_price AS first_price, p2.monthly_price AS second_price FROM ranked r1 JOIN ranked r2 ON r2.account_id = r1.account_id AND r2.rn = 2 JOIN plans p1 ON p1.plan_id = r1.plan_id JOIN plans p2 ON p2.plan_id = r2.plan_id WHERE r1.rn = 1) SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE second_price > first_price)::DOUBLE / count(*) AS upgrade_rate, avg(second_price - first_price) FILTER (WHERE second_price > first_price) AS avg_price_increase_among_upgraders FROM pivoted
